evidence.field: 身 evolution record; entries 合集822正, 集成04025; interpretation
evidence.text: The record lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript and small-seal forms, including oracle-bone 合集822正 and bronze 集成04025. It describes the ancient 身 graph as resembling a woman with a large pregnant abdomen. This is the database's interpretation; the image alone does not establish pregnancy as the graph's first meaning.
evidence.title: 漢字「身」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 / Multi-function Chinese Character Database, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; oracle-bone, bronze, and Warring States examples
evidence.text: The database analyzes early forms as 人 with the abdomen marked, possibly including a navel dot, and proposes 腹部 ‘abdomen’ as the original sense. It cites the oracle-bone use 合集822正 for the king's abdominal illness; bronze inscriptions for body/person, personal action, and era; and Guodian Laozi B strip 8 and Qinghua 程寤 strip 9 for body. It treats 有身 in 詩經·大雅·大明 as ‘pregnant’ and the body and self senses as semantic extensions. The page supplies citation labels but not absolute dates for each example.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 身

evidence.text: The page reproduces Xu Shen's account: 身 means 躳, depicts a person's body, and is analyzed as 从人𠂆聲. CUHK presents this as a historical dictionary account alongside a different analysis of the early graph; it does not confirm that 𠂆 was a phonetic component of the earliest form.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 身

evidence.field: historical dictionary citations and semantic examples
evidence.text: The entry records body/trunk examples from 孟子·告子下 and 楚辭·九歌·國殤; self from 論語·學而; and 有身 from 詩經·大雅·大明, with the latter glossed as pregnancy in its Kangxi quotation. These are textual citations, not independently dated manuscripts, and do not by themselves establish a chronology among all senses.
evidence.title: 身 shēn - 汉典

evidence.field: 2015 draft, section discussing 仁 and 身 pronunciations
evidence.text: The authors report that pre-Qin documents write 仁 ‘kind’ with 身 as phonetic and use this to reconstruct 仁 *ninʔ > nyin > rén and 身 *ni[n] > syin > shēn. This supports a phonetic role for 身 in 仁 and a reconstruction argument; the inspected passage does not name or date a specific manuscript exemplar.
evidence.title: Draft2015-11-08 (Baxter-Sagart, 2015 draft)

evidence.source: Baxter–Sagart 2014 reconstruction table, exact local row supplied in input
evidence.field: local row: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, 身; Mandarin, MC, OC
evidence.text: The exact supplied local row gives 身 Mandarin shēn, MC syin, OC *n̥i[ŋ], gloss ‘body; self’. The notation is preserved as provided. The accessible 2015 draft instead prints *ni[n] > syin > shēn; these are distinct versions/statements and are not silently merged. search_audit.outcome: Inspected exact Xiaoxuetang form record and Commons oracle redraw page with original file, source attribution and CC0 notice; inspected the exact Commons seal redraw page. Separate chardb rights page states restrictive rights, so it was not used as an image asset. Some Commons linked file pages had cache failures.

gaps: The early-graph interpretations remain disputed: Academia Sinica describes a pregnant woman, while CUHK analyzes a person with the abdomen marked and proposes abdomen as the original sense. The reviewed sources do not establish a visually decisive interpretation.
The references give inscription and manuscript identifiers but not absolute dates for every use; no continuous dated graphic lineage or specific corruption sequence was established.

The proposed later semantic steps (abdomen to pregnancy/body to whole person/self) are CUHK's analysis. Individual cited examples support uses, but do not independently prove every semantic transition.
The Shuowen component statement 人 plus 𠂆 as phonetic is a historical account; no reviewed source establishes 𠂆 as a phonetic in the earliest graph.

Exact Unicode Unihan character-specific records for 身 and 申 were inaccessible. The exact supplied local row for 身 is preserved as local data; no 申 sound-component analysis was needed for the supported graph history.

The 2014 Baxter–Sagart table PDF was found but could not be opened. Its supplied local row is not presented as directly inspected upstream material; the accessible 2015 draft uses a different visible OC notation for 身 and supports the phonetic evidence from 身 in 仁.
A whole-graph loan of 身 for a pronoun was not established. CUHK describes self/reflexive meanings as semantic extensions; this research does not classify them as borrowing.

The Commons oracle and seal files are modern vector redrawings rather than artifact photographs. The seal example clarifies a later script form but is not evidence for the disputed earliest interpretation.
